title: The Prom of Lake Minnow
premise: Rosalind Amberdale has spent two years at Lake Minnow Academy being nobody, but a forced partnership with her nemesis Theo Vance for the Founders' Project drags her into the school's buried history: a scholarship fund, a decades-old disappearance, and a prom tradition that decides who inherits the academy's hidden endowment. As they dig, Rosalind discovers the vanished founder's heir was never found — and the clues point uncomfortably close to her own adoption. To claim the truth before the school board seals the archives at prom night, she and Theo must enter the championship debate that 'doesn't matter' and win the social war that does, culminating in a prom where Rosalind publicly claims her inheritance, exposes the board's cover-up, and chooses her found family over the bloodline she finally understands.
about_author: Wendell Hartwell is a former boarding school debate coach who spent seven years teaching at small academies tucked into lake country, collecting the rumors students swore him to secrecy over. He writes young adult fiction from a cabin with unreliable Wi-Fi and a reliable dog named Minnow.

chapters.title: Locker Shut, Head Down
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. We meet her survival system at Lake Minnow Academy: perfect grades, zero friends, total invisibility — until she accidentally beats Theo Vance in class and shatters his spotlight. The teacher announces paired Founders' Projects; Rosalind and Theo are matched. Emotional beat: the cost of hiding, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: Nemesis Terms
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Theo negotiate a hostile truce in the library, dividing research on founder Edmund Lake's vanished endowment. A misfiled ledger reveals the scholarship fund Rosalind receives was funded by a trust that legally requires an heir. Emotional beat: reluctant respect disguised as bickering.

chapters.title: The Archive That Isn't
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo uses his social capital to get them into the restricted wing, where they find the 1974 file of a missing student — a scholarship kid who disappeared the same year the trust was frozen. Headmistress Corliss catches them but, strangely, lets them go with a warning. Emotional beat: first real danger, first real ally.

chapters.title: Adoption Papers and Prom Dresses
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Home for fall break, Rosalind compares her adoption date to the missing student's disappearance and finds them weeks apart. Her adoptive mother admits she was told to keep certain questions unasked. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of Rosalind's identity.

chapters.title: Debate Season Opens
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. To access the board's sealed records, the pair must win the Founders' Debate Championship — the prize is archival access, which is why the board rigs the draw against them. Theo sacrifices his own social standing by partnering publicly with Rosalind. Emotional beat: Theo chooses her over his inheritance of popularity.

chapters.title: The Corliss Tapes
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Headmistress Corliss reveals she was the missing student's roommate and has spent thirty years unable to prove what happened: the board declared the heir dead to seize the trust. She gives them a partial recording, warning that prom night is when the seal becomes permanent. Emotional beat: grief, and the weight of borrowed courage.

chapters.title: Semifinals and Sabotage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Rivals steal their evidence file; Theo's old friends turn on him. Rebuilding their case from memory the night before, Rosalind and Theo finally say the true thing out loud — they're not partners of convenience anymore. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They win the debate with a case built entirely on the trust's own legal language, earning archive access — and discovering the board has moved the seal-up to prom night, hours early. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Prom of Lake Minnow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At prom, Rosalind presents the completed proof — the missing heir was declared dead falsely, and the heir's trail leads to her own adoption. The board's chair confesses on the gym floor as students record everything. Emotional beat: the invisible girl made unmistakably visible.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Keeps
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, weeks later. The trust is restored; Rosalind renames the scholarship for the missing student and declines to leave her adoptive mother's home for the estate. She and Theo, now openly inseparable, plan next year's project together. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined — what you choose over what you're owed.
